name: liquid H2S at 188 K (an estimated index)
paper: the estimate's inputs: C. and M. Cuthbertson, Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A 83 (1910) 171, for H2S's gas dispersion; E. W. Lemmon and R. Span, J. Chem. Eng. Data 51 (2006) 785, DOI 10.1021/je050186n, as the NIST Chemistry WebBook gives it, for the liquid's density
source: a Lorentz–Lorenz estimate, not a measurement (decision-p14-t49h-gas-index §2.5 and A.4): view/atmosphere/rayleigh.ts's GAS_DISPERSION row for H2S (C. and M. Cuthbertson, Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A 83 (1910) 171), stated at 273.15 K and 101325 Pa with Z = 1.00066, measured over 486.1–656.3 nm and extrapolated beyond, unscaled (c = 1), at 29.11633 mol/l at 187.7 K, the NIST Chemistry WebBook's saturated liquid (SRD 69, after E. W. Lemmon and R. Span, J. Chem. Eng. Data 51 (2006) 785, DOI 10.1021/je050186n, density uncertain by 0.1% in the liquid; https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/fluid.cgi?Action=Data&Wide=on&ID=C7783064&Type=SatP&Digits=7&THigh=187.71&TLow=187.7&TInc=0.01&RefState=DEF&TUnit=K&PUnit=MPa&DUnit=mol%2Fl&HUnit=kJ%2Fmol&WUnit=m%2Fs&VisUnit=uPa*s&STUnit=N%2Fm, SHA-256 43945332d433fac4e2fb492644a740fa14e726ce79b4a4b0ee5b96f7c4cc1d16, fetched 2026-10-16), the registry row's triple point. Bleekrode 1884 measured the liquid at the sodium lines (Proc. R. Soc. Lond. 37, 339, p. 351; public domain; the archive.org copy, its text, https://archive.org/download/paper-doi-10_1098_rspl_1884_0039/paper-doi-10_1098_rspl_1884_0039_djvu.txt, SHA-256 2d7fa8df25c59fbaec00207ed98b89ba7b53e2264e163b5b8065a0375377048d, fetched 2026-10-16), in 1879 with the compression pump and later in a Faraday tube under its own pressure: 1.380 at 12.5 °C (23.62573 mol/l), the estimate less it −0.0100; 1.384 at 18.5 °C (23.21197 mol/l), the estimate less it −0.0212, at the WebBook's densities (https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/fluid.cgi?Action=Data&Wide=on&ID=C7783064&Type=SatP&Digits=7&THigh=291.65&TLow=285.65&TInc=6&RefState=DEF&TUnit=K&PUnit=MPa&DUnit=mol%2Fl&HUnit=kJ%2Fmol&WUnit=m%2Fs&VisUnit=uPa*s&STUnit=N%2Fm, SHA-256 82c2f290c1512b903d3e410d27f2288934f86d2a6805fcc5037c064ebc340d12, fetched 2026-10-16). They run the wrong way with temperature, the warmer liquid's index the higher, so neither anchors the file; both are recorded. This is the one molecular liquid of the method's record whose estimate runs low at every measurement, by 0.010–0.021, far beyond the measurements' errors (Kr's and Xe's run low too, by under 0.003, as the heavy atoms' liquids do). licence: estimated values from the gas dispersion view/atmosphere/rayleigh.ts cites and the NIST Chemistry WebBook's density (NIST Standard Reference Data), with two measured values cited as facts; no data set is copied
reduction: n = √((1 + 2x) ÷ (1 − x)) with x = R(λ) ρ_m, the gas's molar refraction at the liquid's density, unscaled (c = 1), evaluated at each wavelength of 380–780 nm every 5 nm, to six significant figures; k = 0: the liquid is colourless in the visible. The stated band: −0.005 and +0.021 in n, the estimate likely low, as against Bleekrode's values
standIn: a non-absorbing liquid whose real index is a Lorentz–Lorenz estimate from the gas's dispersion at the liquid's density, since its measured values contradict themselves: 1.380 at 286 K and 1.384 at 292 K, at 589 nm, 0.010 and 0.021 above the estimate there; at 188 K the estimate is 1.498 at 380 nm, 1.472 at 550 nm and 1.462 at 780 nm, within +0.021 and -0.005, likely low
